questions.cardText:
[Cultural Studies] What is the mythological origin of the Spring Festival?
A. To scare away a monster
B. To welcome the dragon king
C. To celebrate the Jade Emperor
Answer: A. The Spring Festival, or Chinese New Year, originates from the legend of the monster Nian. Villagers discovered that Nian was afraid of loud noises, bright lights, and the color red. To protect themselves, they lit firecrackers, decorated their homes with red banners, and stayed up all night, practices that evolved into modern Spring Festival customs.
questions.de: Welches Ungeheuer der chinesischen Sage, das laute Geräusche und die Farbe Rot fürchtet, sollen die Böller und roten Dekorationen des Frühlingsfests (chinesisches Neujahr) vertreiben?
questions.en: Which monster of Chinese legend, afraid of loud noises and the colour red, are the firecrackers and red decorations of the Spring Festival (Chinese New Year) said to scare away?

timeline.labelEn: Earliest written sources describing the nian as a creature appear (early 20th century)
timeline.labelDe: Die ältesten schriftlichen Quellen, die den Nian als Wesen beschreiben, erscheinen (frühes 20. Jahrhundert)

questions.notes: Card's legend matches Wikipedia's Nian article (fears red and loud noise; red lanterns, scrolls, firecrackers). Wikipedia notes written sources for the nian as a creature only date from the early 20th century, so its antiquity as folklore is unclear.

questions.cardText:
[Geography] What is the capital city of Australia?
A. Sydney B. Melbourne C. Canberra
Answer: C.
questions.en: What is the capital city of Australia?
